svg.title: Funding the Gap and Getting Paid
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-funding-and-payment-roadmap; chapter number: 12; title: Funding the Gap and Getting Paid; subtitle: From financing choice to a proper invoice that starts the payment clock; caption: A contractor typically works about 30 days, invoices, then waits roughly another 30. Debra Smith calls 3% to 5% a fair factoring fee, flags anything over 5%, and cites RTS Financial at 2.5%.; assumptions note: The four-week sequencing is an organizing frame and no practitioner testified to a weekly schedule. Progress payments run 80% for large and 95% for small businesses, and performance-based payments reach up to 90% of contract value (Acquisition Pro Tips).; note: Sources - Debra Smith (NusotbSsCa4), Business Cash Now with Chris Curtin (4V1zq5q3VuQ), Mobilization Capital (oOQSsJO94kM), Acquisition Pro Tips (WXCymE9NjBg, cdachjXPX3k), Tris10 @ MeND (weLOISkZc5k, yXqp5I7wQK0).; chart type: timeline_roadmap; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Pick the Funding Tool; deliverable: Factoring for services and credit cards for products (Debra Smith), or a mobilization lender against a signed contract or Notice to Proceed; gate: Margin covers the fee, since 5% to 7% low-bid margins leave nothing for financing (Business Cash Now); week: Week 2; title: Lock the Supplier; deliverable: Supplier terms in hand with agency name and POC kept confidential; gate: A sub demanding the agency name and POC before the PO is a signal to walk (Debra Smith); week: Week 3; title: Ship and Invoice in WAWF; deliverable: Combo for supplies or Invoice 2-in-1 for services, a Z on the final shipment, and photos plus carrier proof of delivery; gate: Ship-to DoDAAC is not the admin DoDAAC (Acquisition Pro Tips); week: Week 4; title: Chase the Payment; deliverable: My Invoice opened every Friday, and rejected invoices copied with only the failed field fixed; gate: A proper invoice starts the 30-day prompt payment clock, with late interest quoted at 4.6%
